_doc:
THE SHARED SEGMENT-SPLITTING PRIMITIVE (jas_dioxus/src/algorithms/arrangement.rs, JasSwift/Sources/Algorithms/Arrangement.swift). It is the first stage of BOTH the planar-graph extractor and the boolean ring normalizer, so it is the most production-reachable geometry in the tree -- and until this family it had NO cross-language corpus at all: its entire assurance was 11 Rust tests and 11 Swift tests MIRRORED BY HAND, which is agreement-by-transcription, not equivalence.

Two entry points are gated, because both are public and both are called by both consumers:

  split_points(a1,a2,b1,b2) -> [(p, s, t)]  -- every arrangement-relevant meeting of the two segments: proper crossings, T-junctions, endpoint coincidences, and the two ends of a collinear overlap. `s` is p's parameter on a, `t` its parameter on b.

  add_or_find_vertex(verts, pt) -> index    -- the linear-search vertex dedup that fuses split points into shared vertices.

EXPECTATIONS ARE HAND-DERIVED from the documented predicate and epsilon policy (VERT_EPS 1e-9 absolute; PARAM_EPS 1e-9 on the normalized parameter; DENOM_EPS 1e-12 on the raw 2x2 determinant; COLLINEAR_EPS 1e-9 perpendicular distance). Every `derivation` field carries the arithmetic. No expectation was produced by running either port.

THE `endpoint` FIELD IS NOT DECORATION. The module's contract says a returned point is TAKEN FROM an existing endpoint whenever one of the parameters sits at an endpoint, `exactly`, rather than re-derived by a1 + s*(a2-a1) -- and that exactness is what lets the caller's dedup fuse a T-junction into one vertex instead of two. A tolerance comparison is blind to the difference between (5.0, 0.0) and (4.999999999999999, 0.0), so each result reports WHICH of the four input endpoints its point is BIT-IDENTICAL to (first match in the order a1, a2, b1, b2), or null. That field is compared as a string and admits no tolerance.

COORDINATES ARE SMALL AND MOSTLY INTEGRAL on purpose (docs/CHECKERS.md section 4, the hex-bit-pattern rule): serde_json mis-parses about one shortest-round-trip f64 literal in ten by an ulp, so a fixture full of random doubles would put the two ports on different inputs. Where a vector needs a value inside an epsilon band, it is chosen so that the OUTPUT is insensitive to a one-ulp parse difference -- either the value is snapped away entirely, or it is echoed and compared under the 1e-12 tolerance, which is ~10^13 ulps wide at these magnitudes.
_tolerance_why: Both ports run the same divisions on the same small-integer inputs, so agreement should be bit-exact; 1e-12 is set well above one ulp at these magnitudes (~1e-16) and well below every discriminating difference the vectors encode, the narrowest of which is the 1e-9 PARAM_EPS band itself.

vectors.name: proper_crossing_with_unequal_parameters
vectors.derivation: SEPARATES s FROM t, which the equal-parameter crossing above cannot: a port that swapped the two would compare green on every 0.5/0.5 vector. a=(0,0)-(4,0), b=(1,-3)-(1,1). denom = 4*4 - 0*0 = 16. dxab = 0-1 = -1, dyab = 0-(-3) = 3. s = (0*3 - 4*(-1))/16 = 4/16 = 0.25. t = (4*3 - 0*(-1))/16 = 12/16 = 0.75. p = (0 + 0.25*4, 0) = (1,0), re-derived.

vectors.name: t_junction_takes_b_start_exactly
vectors.derivation: b's START lands in a's interior. a=(0,0)-(10,0), b=(5,0)-(5,5). denom = 10*5 - 0*0 = 50. dxab = -5, dyab = 0. s = (0*0 - 5*(-5))/50 = 0.5. t = (10*0 - 0*(-5))/50 = 0. t is AT an endpoint, s is not, so the point must be b1 itself and bit-identically so -- not 5.0000000001.

vectors.name: t_junction_takes_b_end_exactly
vectors.derivation: THE MIRROR OF THE ROW ABOVE, and NO test in either port's hand-mirrored set reaches it: the `t == 1 -> p = b2` branch of the crossing case. b's END lands in a's interior. a=(0,0)-(10,0), b=(5,5)-(5,0). denom = 10*(-5) - 0*0 = -50. dxab = 0-5 = -5, dyab = 0-5 = -5. s = (0*(-5) - (-5)*(-5))/(-50) = (-25)/(-50) = 0.5. t = (10*(-5) - 0*(-5))/(-50) = 1.0. So p = b2 = (5,0), bit-exact.

vectors.name: t_junction_takes_a_end_exactly
vectors.derivation: The `s == 1 -> p = a2` branch of the CROSSING case, also unreached by the hand-mirrored tests (they reach it only through the collinear branch). a=(0,0)-(10,0), b=(10,-5)-(10,5). denom = 10*10 - 0*0 = 100. dxab = 0-10 = -10, dyab = 0-(-5) = 5. s = (0*5 - 10*(-10))/100 = 1.0. t = (10*5 - 0*(-10))/100 = 0.5. p = a2 = (10,0).

vectors.name: endpoint_coincidence_at_the_shared_vertex
vectors.derivation: a=(0,0)-(10,0), b=(0,0)-(0,10). denom = 100, dxab = dyab = 0, so s = t = 0. Both parameters are at an endpoint; the point is a1 (which is also b1 -- the reported endpoint name is the FIRST match in the order a1,a2,b1,b2).

vectors.name: parameter_just_inside_the_snap_band_snaps_to_the_endpoint
vectors.derivation: PARAM_EPS = 1e-9. a=(0,0)-(1,0), b=(5e-10,-1)-(5e-10,1). denom = 1*2 - 0*0 = 2. dxab = 0 - 5e-10, dyab = 0-(-1) = 1. s = (0*1 - 2*(-5e-10))/2 = 5e-10, which is <= PARAM_EPS, so s snaps to EXACTLY 0 and the point becomes a1 = (0,0) -- NOT (5e-10, 0). t = (1*1 - 0)/2 = 0.5. The output carries no trace of the 5e-10 input, so this vector is immune to a one-ulp parse difference.

vectors.name: parameter_just_outside_the_snap_band_stays_interior
vectors.derivation: THE OTHER SIDE OF THE SAME BAND, so the pair pins where the band ENDS rather than merely that one exists. Same construction with 2e-9 > PARAM_EPS: s = 2e-9 does not snap, so the point is re-derived as (0 + 2e-9*1, 0) and matches no input endpoint. t = 0.5.

vectors.name: parallel_but_not_collinear_has_no_meeting
vectors.derivation: a=(0,0)-(10,0), b=(0,1)-(10,1). denom = 10*0 - 0*10 = 0, so the parallel branch runs. Perpendicular distance from b1 to a's line is 1, far above COLLINEAR_EPS, so the pair is rejected.

vectors.name: collinear_partial_overlap_reports_both_overlap_ends
vectors.derivation: a covers x in [0,10]; b covers [4,20]; the overlap is [4,10]. len2a = 100. tb1 = 4*10/100 = 0.4, tb2 = 20*10/100 = 2.0. start = max(0.4, 0) = 0.4, end = min(2.0, 1) = 1.0. u=0.4 equals tb1, so the point is b1 = (4,0) exactly, and t = project(b1..b2, (4,0)) = 0. u=1.0 snaps to s=1, so the point is a2 = (10,0), and t = ((10-4)*16)/256 = 0.375.

vectors.name: collinear_overlap_is_independent_of_b_direction
vectors.derivation: THE SAME SPANS AS THE ROW ABOVE with b reversed, and it pins t as well as p -- the hand-mirrored test for this case asserts only the two points, so a port whose t was measured from the wrong end of b would pass it. b=(20,0)-(4,0): tb1 = 2.0, tb2 = 0.4, lo=0.4, hi=2.0, so start=0.4 end=1.0 as before. u=0.4 matches tb2 now, so the point is b2 = (4,0) and t = project((20,0)..(4,0), (4,0)) = ((4-20)*(-16))/256 = 1.0. u=1.0 gives a2 = (10,0) with t = ((10-20)*(-16))/256 = 0.625.

vectors.name: collinear_contained_span_reports_the_inner_ends
vectors.derivation: b sits strictly inside a, so BOTH of b's endpoints split a and neither overlap end is clamped. tb1 = 0.3, tb2 = 0.7; both are interior, so s is 0.3 and 0.7 and the points are b1 and b2 with t = 0 and 1.

vectors.name: collinear_touching_at_one_point_reports_one_point
vectors.derivation: a covers [0,10], b covers [10,20]: the spans meet only at x=10. tb1 = 1.0, tb2 = 2.0, start = 1.0, end = min(2.0,1) = 1.0, and |end-start| <= PARAM_EPS collapses the two overlap ends to one. s snaps to 1, so the point is a2 = (10,0); t = project((10,0)..(20,0), (10,0)) = 0.

vectors.name: collinear_disjoint_spans_have_no_meeting
vectors.derivation: a covers [0,10], b covers [20,30]. tb1 = 2.0, tb2 = 3.0, start = 2.0, end = min(3.0, 1) = 1.0, and end < start - PARAM_EPS, so nothing is reported.

vectors.name: collinear_span_entirely_before_a_has_no_meeting
vectors.derivation: THE OTHER SIDE of the disjointness test, which the hand-mirrored set does not carry: b lies BEFORE a rather than after it, so the clamp runs the other way. tb1 = -3.0, tb2 = -2.0; start = max(-3,0) = 0.0, end = min(-2,1) = -2.0, and end < start - PARAM_EPS rejects.

vectors.name: collinear_full_retrace_reports_both_endpoints
vectors.derivation: A segment and its exact reverse -- the self-overlap a retraced spike produces. a=(5,10)-(5,5), b=(5,5)-(5,10). len2a = 25. tb1 = ((5-5)*0 + (5-10)*(-5))/25 = 1.0, tb2 = 0.0. lo=0, hi=1, so start=0 and end=1: s=0 gives a1=(5,10) with t = project((5,5)..(5,10),(5,10)) = 1, and s=1 gives a2=(5,5) with t=0.

vectors.name: collinear_overlap_off_the_axes
vectors.derivation: EVERY OTHER COLLINEAR VECTOR IN THIS FILE AND IN BOTH PORTS' TEST SETS IS AXIS-ALIGNED, so the projection arithmetic is exercised with one of dx,dy always zero. a=(0,0)-(8,6) (length 10), b=(4,3)-(12,9). denom = 8*6 - 6*8 = 0; both of b's endpoints are exactly on a's line. len2a = 100. tb1 = (4*8 + 3*6)/100 = 0.5, tb2 = (12*8 + 9*6)/100 = 1.5. start = 0.5, end = 1.0. u=0.5 matches tb1 so the point is b1 = (4,3) with t = 0; u=1.0 snaps to s=1 so the point is a2 = (8,6) with t = ((8-4)*8 + (6-3)*6)/100 = 0.5.

vectors.name: zero_length_a_splits_nothing
vectors.derivation: DEGENERATE, and it pairs with the next row to pin an ASYMMETRY that neither port's tests state. a is a point sitting on b's interior. denom = 0, so the parallel branch runs, and len2a = 0 rejects immediately -- a degenerate `a` never reports a meeting, even one that is geometrically there.

vectors.name: zero_length_b_on_a_interior_does_split
vectors.derivation: THE ASYMMETRY: the same degenerate configuration with the roles swapped DOES report. b is the point (5,0) on a's interior. denom = 0, len2a = 100 > 0, both distances are 0 so the pair is collinear, and tb1 = tb2 = 0.5 collapses to one overlap end. s = 0.5, the point is b1 = (5,0), and t = 0 because project_param returns 0 for a degenerate segment.

vectors.name: sub_denom_eps_pair_is_treated_as_collinear
vectors.derivation: DENOM_EPS = 1e-12 on the RAW determinant, so the branch it guards is reachable only at small scale. a=(0,0)-(1e-6,0); b=(2.5e-7,0)-(7.5e-7,1e-13). denom = 1e-6*1e-13 - 0 = 1e-19, below DENOM_EPS, so the PARALLEL branch runs; both perpendicular distances (0 and 1e-13) are under COLLINEAR_EPS, so the pair is collinear with tb1 = 0.25 and tb2 = 0.75 and TWO overlap ends are reported. This is discriminating: a port that took the crossing branch instead would compute s=0.25, t=0 and report ONE point.

vectors.name: add_or_find_dedups_within_vert_eps
vectors.derivation: VERT_EPS = 1e-9, STRICTLY less than. Starting from an empty list: (0,0) is pushed at 0; (10,0) is 10 away so it is pushed at 1; (0,0) again matches index 0; (10,5e-10) is 5e-10 from index 1, inside the band, so it returns 1 WITHOUT being stored; (10,2e-9) is outside the band so it is pushed at 2. The final list is what the caller's topology is built on, so it is reported alongside the indices.

vectors.name: add_or_find_first_match_wins_over_a_nearer_one
vectors.derivation: THE ORDER-DEPENDENCE WITNESS. Two stored vertices are both inside the band around the query, and the FIRST one is FARTHER. The contract is a linear search that returns the first match, so the answer is 0; a port that returned the NEAREST match would answer 1 and every other vector in this family would still be green. Nothing is appended, so the stored list comes back unchanged.

vectors.name: add_or_find_measures_against_the_stored_representative
vectors.derivation: Dedup is measured against what is STORED, not against the last point seen, so tolerance does not chain. (0,0) is pushed at 0. (0,6e-10) is inside the band around index 0, so it returns 0 and is NOT stored. (0,1.2e-9) is 1.2e-9 from the stored (0,0) -- outside the band -- so it is pushed at 1, even though it is only 6e-10 from the point that preceded it. A port that had stored the second point, or that compared against the previous input, would answer [0,0,0] and hold two vertices instead of three positions.
